speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I am Dr. Agent. To help me understand your condition, can you describe the appearance of the rash on your scalp and forehead, and tell me how long you have had it?

speaker: Patient
text: 3-month-old boy. The parents report that the rash has been present for several weeks, noting that it sometimes appears red and scaly, especially during cold weather. The patient was born at 36 weeks' gestation and has been generally healthy since. The patient's father has a history of psoriasis.

speaker: Doctor
text: Does the rash cause significant itching or discomfort for the baby, and have you noticed any scaling on other areas of the body, such as the diaper area or skin folds?

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Rash on scalp and forehead. I also have Erythematous patches, Greasy yellow scales, Worse in cold weather.

speaker: Doctor
text: The greasy yellow scales and involvement of the scalp and forehead in an infant are classic signs. To confirm, have you noticed any crusting or scaling around the baby's ears or in the diaper area?

speaker: Patient
text: Past medical history: Premature birth (36 weeks), otherwise generally healthy. Family history of psoriasis. Social history: The patient is 3 months old, so the social history is not applicable.

speaker: Doctor
text: The presence of greasy yellow scales on the scalp and forehead, worsening in cold weather, is highly characteristic of infantile seborrheic dermatitis, often called cradle cap. Given the classic presentation and lack of severe symptoms like intense itching or involvement of the diaper area, I am confident in my assessment. DIAGNOSIS READY: Infantile Seborrheic Dermatitis
